rules.selection_criteria: Review association, known-response N/exclusions, within-group variation, shuffle stability and graphical legibility together; never select solely by the largest observed gap.
rules.status: Exploratory candidate screening on an already observed temporal test; all declared results retained, no confirmatory selection claim.
rules.selection: Binary candidates: both inputs in sim/nao. Numeric age: finite age and group in sim/nao. No outcome-based restriction or extra subsampling.
rules.model: Historical fixed XGBoost reconstructed in section 5; same forty inputs, no extra fit or calibration in this section.
rules.orders: A fresh default_rng(42) stream for each candidate cohort; fifty consecutive draws, paired marginal/within orders in each repeat. No seed search.
rules.within: Restore original inputs; filter the repeat order by the original fixed group. Groups are other inputs, never the death outcome or the permuted input itself.
rules.loss: Log loss of float64 positive-class probabilities; natural logarithm and epsilon-float64 clipping; true outcomes and other thirty-nine inputs stay at recipient positions.
rules.baseline: Own original loss for every cohort and group. Different known-response cohorts cannot be interpreted as a common-population feature ranking.
rules.gap: Paired marginal-minus-within increase in log loss. Positive means larger marginal importance here; not proof of estimator improvement or full conditional validity.
rules.sd: Sample SD across fifty shuffles, ddof=1; fixed model and observed recipients. Not a confidence interval or population uncertainty.
rules.association: Pearson/phi for known binary pairs, point-biserial Pearson for continuous age and binary group; association between inputs, not association with death or causal evidence.
rules.relative_percent: Difference divided by own baseline times one hundred; change in loss, never a change in death probability or classification-error percentage.
rules.plot: Binary plots are exact aggregate counts of the first registered shuffle, not a selected favorable repeat. Conditional percentages divide by each fixed-group N. No synthetic individual records.
rules.limits: Preserving one pair does not preserve the other input dependencies. All known combinations and any original recording problems remain part of the observed data.
